newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Optus announces new management team.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Optus announces new management team.

text.p: Australian telephone carrier Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Thursday it had organised a new management structure following the appointment of new chief executive officer Peter Howell-Davies last week.
Optus said Optus Communications chief operating officer Phil Jacobs would take on the additional responsibility of chief operating officer of Optus Vision, Optus' pay television arm.
The Optus Vision senior management team led by Dick Simpson remained unchanged and would report to Jacobs, Optus said.
It said Jacobs would shortly announce details of the Optus Communications senior management team reporting to him.
Optus said that reporting to Howell-Davies also would be Stephen Stefanovski, currently acting chief financial officer and Norman Gillespie, director of finance.

Gillespie, who was previously director of planning at Cable and Wireless Plc, would also take have responsibility for the financial aspects of the integration of Optus Vision into the Optus group, following the merger in April, Optus said.
It said it had created the position of director, strategy and regulation, which will be held by Christopher Weston, a former executive at Mercury Communications, a unit of Cable and Wireless (C&W).
Optus said Weston was closely involved with the formation of Cable & Wireless Communications Plc, which was created after the merger between Mercury and three cable groups.
It said existing directors George Webster and Sam Mostyn would remain in their respective roles, while the company would soon appoint a new legal director.
Acting as key advisor to Howell-Davies would be Ted Pretty, currently a member of the Optus board.
Optus is 24.5 percent owned by Cable & Wireless, which is expected to up its stake to 49 percent with the expcted purchase of BellSouth Corp's 24.5 percent stake.
The remaining Optus shareholdings are owned by Australian institutions.
